items.name: Ankush Rana
items.title: SR. Software Tester
items.text:
Working with Rakesh, was eye-opening because he refused to let me stay in the UI automation box. I came in comfortable with Playwright and frontend testing, but he kept pushing: "Why are we testing this at the UI layer when the data's wrong at the source?" That question led me down the BigQuery rabbit hole, and suddenly I'm writing validation scripts that catch bugs before they even hit the frontend.

What I appreciated most: he treated database knowledge—whether it's MongoDB or BigQuery—as essential to QA, not optional. Most PMs would hand you a task. He'd ask why we were testing something, which forced me to think about architecture instead of just executing scripts. By the end of our time together, I wasn't just an automation engineer bouncing between Playwright and Python queries—I understood the why behind both.

He modeled how to ask the right questions. He had this way of making it obvious that if you're only testing what you see, you're missing half the story. Worked with great managers before, but he's the one who changed how I think about testing fundamentally. That's made me a better tester.
